items.t: Said he is proud of what was achieved over the years for working people in Washington, including better benefits, a safer workplace and higher wages.

items.t: Is described as taking pride in being a spokesperson for working families and a champion of collective bargaining rights, and as believing workers' rights are human rights.
items.q: He prides himself on being a spokesperson for working families, champion of collective bargaining rights, and a firm believer that workers’ rights are human rights.

items.t: Said he joins the concern neighbors have expressed about the upcoming closure of the Fred Meyer at South 72nd and Pacific.
items.q: “I join in the concern so many of our neighbors have expressed to me regarding the upcoming closure of the Fred Meyer located at South 72 nd and Pacific.

record.t: Served the 29th Legislative District since 1993, first as a State Representative for 18 years and then as a Senator since 2011.
record.q: Senator Steve Conway has served the 29th Legislative District since 1993, first as a State Representative for 18 years, and then as a Senator since 2011.

record.t: Served as President Pro Tempore and on the Labor & Commerce and Ways & Means committees.
record.q: In addition to serving in a leadership role as President Pro Tempore, he serves on the Labor & Commerce and Ways & Means committees.

record.t: Served as Chair of the Labor & Commerce Committee in the House and as vice chair in the Senate.
record.q: I have been a member of that committee in one way or another since I first arrived in Olympia back in 1993. I served as Chair in the House and vice chair in the Senate

record.t: Announced he will not seek reelection after 34 years of service in the Washington State Legislature.
record.q: Sen. Steve Conway (D-South Tacoma) announced Wednesday that after 34 years of service in the Washington State Legislature, he will not seek reelection.
